final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was provided. The actor mainly reframed the same record more narrowly and conceded the key deficiency: the present admissible evidence still does not show disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case. Under the stated policy, that missing predicate is an unresolved compliance condition, not merely a reporting caveat. A caveated certification posture may be a more accurate description of the business debate, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the caveat itself is the unsatisfied policy requirement. General governance guidance and aggregate readiness evidence remain contextual support only and cannot substitute for the specific launch-approval predicate.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance for the insurance claims triage limitation before launch.
The insurance claims triage gap remains material because the segment is named in two carrier pilot commitments and legal review is still open.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the separate policy predicate for a material limitation in a named launch use case.
The actor's narrowed framing is more accurate than a claim of clean compliance, but it does not cure the unresolved policy requirement.
